utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-96-23/2-I, the Prosecutor versus Dragan Zelenovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Zelenovic, I take it you're Mr. Zelenovic. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to have the appearances. Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff, I appear for the Prosecution, together with case manager, Sebastiaan van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DER SPOEL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Tjarda Van der Spoel, duty counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Van der Spoel. Mr. Zelenovic, I take it that you discussed with counsel -- that you discussed with counsel the purpose of the proceedings today, that is you make your first appearance before this Tribunal and later on you'll be invited to tell us whether you consider yourself guilty or not guilty. That's the main purpose of this hearing. And then if there are any other issues as far as detention is concerned, about your health is concerned, you could raise them after we have done this. Mr. Zelenovic, one of the first things I have to verify is that you are represented, and I do see that Mr. Van der Spoel is with you today and he just -- when saying that he was duty counsel, we understood this, that he has been appointed by the Registrar to be duty counsel today. Is that -- do you want to say anything about your representation by Mr. Van der Spoel today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. Normal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you received the indictment in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you understand the content of the indictment -- there must be something. Did you understand the content of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have fully understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there was some interference. Mr. Zelenovic, you have the right to have the whole indictment read out in full to you. Do you want to exercise that right or do you want to waive this right? If you want to exercise that right, I'll ask the registrar to read aloud each count of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll come later to the several counts of the indictment. By the way, you don't have to keep standing all the time. If you'd rather sit down, which is more comfortable to you because it will take some time, please then be seated. Mr. Zelenovic, pursuant to Rule 62(A)(iii) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, you have the right to enter a plea, a plea of guilty or a plea of not guilty, on each count today, but you also may choose to enter such a plea within 30 days of this initial appearance. I don't know whether you discussed this with counsel and whether you decided whether you would like to enter a plea today or whether you would rather wait until a later moment within 30 days. What is your choice? There's no need for every single answer to stand up. That's ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have decided to plead in one month's time. I have not got a counsel. I haven't consulted counsel, so I'm not ready to plead today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then -- yes. So you would take your time. We'll then schedule another hearing in which you'll be given an opportunity to enter a plea. Therefore, we don't have to go through all the counts of the indictment at this moment; you have delayed the plea. Mr. Zelenovic, there are a few other matters then which I'd like to raise. First of all, I'd like to inform you that the Prosecution in this case has filed a request before the Referral Bench, which is a Chamber of three Judges, a bench of three Judges, asking that these Judges decide that your case will be referred to the authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina, so asking that this Tribunal will decide that finally you'll have to stand trial in Bosnia and Herzegovina, rather than in The Hague. I just wanted to inform you about that so that you do not leave here with the expectation that your case will be heard anyway by this Tribunal. Another matter I have to raise is your pre-trial custody. Upon your initial appearance, your custody is ordered, you'll be in pre-trial detention, but you may file an application for provisional release pursuant to Rule 65 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal. And if you'd like to file such a request, then stand-by counsel will be able to assist you in this matter. Another matter I would like to briefly raise is that within 30 days of this Initial Appearance, the Prosecution will disclose to the Defence all the material that supports the indictment against you that will be sent to counsel, but it will also be disclosed to your counsel in your own language. That means you can read it; it will be in your language therefore as well. Further, but this is mainly addressing Mr. Van der Spoel, your counsel will have an opportunity to file within a 30-day period of time any preliminary motions, at least on from the date when this supporting material to the indictment has been disclosed to him. You're still standing, and as far as I'm concerned, you may be seated, Mr. Zelenovic. Mr. Zelenovic, I'll now ask your counsel and the Prosecution, having heard that a plea will not be entered today, if there's any other matter the Prosecution would like to raise at this hearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, just an information. It -- we actually were prepared to provide the supporting material today, but because we have only here today the duty counsel and not the permanent counsel, we thought it better to wait until we have the name of the permanent counsel. It's much more practical to disclose it once to this counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Isn't it right that the Rules in respect of the time limits for the filing of preliminary motions have been recently changed only a couple of weeks ago, and that the disclosure obligations remain but that the 30-day period of time - that's at least what is in the back of my mind - waits -- does not start until -- until duty counsel is -- is replaced by permanent counsel, at least other counsel. This has the advantage, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, that the accused can already start reading the material. So therefore, I don't know whether there's any need to delay the disclosure, even if duty counsel would not immediately start acting on it in full detail. But at least then the disclosure is there. I see, Mr. Van der Spoel, you're looking in the Rules. I think, as a matter of fact, that these -- I don't even know -- I have to be carefully because I think the amended rule enters into force, I think, eight days after it has been published or something like that, but there is something in the back of my mind which says that there might be -- or am I mistaken? It's still possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I'm actually not aware of this change, but Mr. Van Hooydonk is looking for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the change is there it is the most recent one, so that's from last month.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We will check it and disclose this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps I mixed up a few things, but I -- therefore --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We definitely have the material together to be disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think as a matter of fact nothing opposes against disclosing it, even if duty counsel would not start working with it, at least - and that's the understanding - that time limits for filing preliminary motions would then start at the appropriate moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DER SPOEL
utterances.text: May I remark on that, please, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DER SPOEL
utterances.text: May I remark on your observation, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DER SPOEL
utterances.text: I discussed the matter yesterday with my client and he was very clear in his position. He thanked me very much for explaining what the proceedings are, but everything concerning his case he would like to have done by his chosen counsel in Bosnia and Herzegovina. He has mentioned the name of the counsel to the registrar. The counsel is not yet on the list of Defence counsel for the ICTY but could be put on that list. It has to be assessed during the -- the Registry is doing the process now, and in the meantime I have been instructed not to do anything. I have discussed the position with the client; of course I have discussed disclosure. The Rules I have are the Rules of the 29th of March 2006. Perhaps there are more recent Rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, that should be them. In other words, I might --

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DER SPOEL
utterances.text: Just to be sure I don't want my client to be put in a position that I have to do something that he doesn't want me to do. So I think it's a sensible suggestion from the side of the Prosecutor to disclose as late as possible that the chosen counsel have more time to prepare his case and see if they can file an objection against the indictment and things like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think as a matter of fact time should remain the same for chosen counsel. It's only that Mr. Zelenovic would deprive himself from an early reading of this material. That's the only thing I had on my mind which that might interest him. Mr. Zelenovic, if the material will be later disclosed to counsel of choice, then it would also mean that you could not read it yet in your own language. If you would say "no" - I would rather start reading even if Mr. Van der Spoel doesn't read at the same time the English version - then please tell us so we could see if it could be resolved in such a way that you do not deprive yourself from looking at the material and that it would not negatively impact on your possibilities to file preliminary motions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel is representing me in court, and he told me, "I shall be representing you. If you take a lawyer in The Hague, then the lawyer won't go to Sarajevo to defend you. So I suggest that I be your Defence counsel because your case will probably come up in Sarajevo, whereas a Sarajevo counsel would not be representing you." That is why I handed everything over to that particular counsel and he told me not to say anything without consulting him. I gave everything to -- I gave the visiting card of the duty counsel to this other counsel so they can get in touch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, perhaps, Mr. Van der Spoel, you'll be able to communicate this specific matter with counsel Mr. Zelenovic has chosen. By the way, Mr. Zelenovic, does your -- does counsel of your choice, does he speak any English or French, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Sarajevo they provided me with a list of lawyers, and I selected that particular person but I didn't ask him. I have his visiting card and I handed over the lawyer's visiting card to the duty counsel, so he is informed of the name and the telephone number and the details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because that could cause some problems in having him assigned to you, even if it were only for the 11 bis proceedings because it's uncertain whether the 11 bis proceedings will, well, go quicker than the development of the proceedings in the case against you. But that's perhaps something to -- Mr. Van der Spoel, to the extent possible, for you to discuss with counsel of choice. Then when you referred to March, that was the date of publication in March. I take it that there is a -- the Rules have been --

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DER SPOEL
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it there have been amendments to the Rules after that. But whenever I find something, I'll make it clear to the parties that every rule is available to everyone. Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, I've got a few questions. First of all, the operative indictment at this moment is an indictment which still bears three names, although I'm aware that the names of two co-accused since then have been in a separate indictment. It seems that the cases of them have been severed but are still on the operative indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's our understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And is -- if this -- is this how you'd like to keep it?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We didn't actually intend to amend it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon? You did not --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We did not intend to amend it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You did, however, for the two others. I think they have got --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- their own indictments.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That's correct. But we actually -- the first one against Mr. Stankovic was amended because the charges were changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the -- in relation to Mr. Jankovic, I seem to recall there was a challenge against the form of the indictment, and that's why we amended it. But I may be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but they were then also separate indictments.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But Mr. Zelenovic will be accompanied by two co-accused who are not appearing anymore in this case?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What we -- what actually can be done, redact -- reductions can be made without having an impact of -- on the indictment as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That's also done occasionally, but that's not really considered an amendment, it's just reductions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's -- then I have one other question for you because within the next 30 days we'll hear a plea entered by Mr. Zelenovic, I take it. And I have one question which is not -- where the indictment perhaps needs some interpretation in order to be fully understood, whereas I think that I'd like to understand what the indictment against the accused is, and I take it that the accused would like to know what the indictment against him is. I'm taking you to page 5 of the amended indictment. In paragraph 5.3, we find a description of soldiers, among them Mr. Dragan Zelenovic, interrogating the women that were detained; then threats expressed against these women; and then it continues that these soldiers, Dragan Zelenovic being among them, gang raped several women during or immediately after the interrogation when they suspected of -- who they suspected of lying. And then it says that in paragraphs 5.4 to 5.6, particularities of some of those assaults are given. And then we find in 5.4, we find what happened to a witness code-named FWS-75, and then it says that she was interrogated, also by Dragan Zelenovic. But when it comes a few lines further down, when it comes to rape, it says that she was raped by ten unidentified soldiers, whereas it seems that in 5.3 you identified Dragan Zelenovic as -- at least that's -- I have some difficulties in understanding it differently. But in 5.4 we find none of the persons suspected of having raped Witness V -- FWS-75 as being identified.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, what we believe -- or rather, it's our position that in relation to the gang rape of the Witness 75, Dragan Zelenovic is responsible for this gang rape, although he himself did not rape that victim because he is -- he and Gojko Jankovic together started. It's one -- it's one event, the gang rape of 75, and Dragan Zelenovic is involved in that as he is, together with Gojko Jankovic, interrogating the woman and then turning her over to the rapists. This is his responsibility in relation to the Witness 75.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So I now --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This is how we see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that although he did not himself commit the rape, as described in further detail in 5.4 --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you keep him responsible under 5.3, individually responsible --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- for his role in the gang rape in which he finally, physically, did not take part and which is described in 5.4?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's how we see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- at least now it's clear to me exactly how to understand the indictment in this respect and also may assist the accused in understanding what he'll be pleading to. Then, Mr. Zelenovic, may I ask you, you arrived in the Detention Unit by now. Do you have any complaints about treatment in the Detention Unit or treatment on your way getting there?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, none at all. Everything is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And then another question is whether there are -- whether you have any concerns about your own health. If you would like to -- if you would prefer to answer that question not in public, please ask me, then we'll turn into private session so that only we will hear any concerns you may raise. But it's up to you. For example, if you have no real health concerns, then it might be --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if there's anything you would like to say about your health which I should know, please, you have an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, nothing at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Is there anything else you'd like to raise, apart from what I raised, health, treatment, is there anything else you would like to bring to my attention prior to the next hearing which will be scheduled within the next 30 days?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Van der Spoel, any matter you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. VAN DER SPOEL
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Zelenovic, this concludes your Initial Appearance, and your hearing will be scheduled in which you will be invited to enter a plea, a guilty plea or a not guilty plea. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: adjourned at 5.32 p.m.
